title: CONDITIONALS PRACTICE & TIPS
description: Master zero, first, second, and third conditional structures.

questions.question: Complete the zero conditional: 'If you heat water to 100°C, it _____ .'
questions.explanation: Zero conditional uses present simple in both clauses for general truths and facts.

questions.question: Choose the correct first conditional: 'If it rains tomorrow, we _____ the picnic.'
questions.explanation: First conditional uses present simple in if-clause and will + base form in main clause for real future possibilities.

questions.question: Complete the second conditional: 'If I _____ a million dollars, I would travel the world.'
questions.explanation: Second conditional uses past simple in if-clause and would + base form in main clause for hypothetical situations.

questions.question: Choose the correct third conditional: 'If she _____ harder, she would have passed the exam.'
questions.explanation: Third conditional uses past perfect in if-clause and would have + past participle in main clause for past hypothetical situations.

questions.question: Complete: 'If you _____ me earlier, I could have helped you.'
questions.explanation: Third conditional for past regret. Past perfect in if-clause, could have + past participle in main clause.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'If I _____ you, I would accept the job offer.'
questions.explanation: Second conditional uses 'were' for all persons in the if-clause, even with 'I'.

questions.question: Complete: 'If you mix red and blue, you _____ purple.'
questions.explanation: Zero conditional for scientific facts. Present simple in both clauses.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'If he _____ the train, he would be here by now.'
questions.explanation: Third conditional for past hypothetical situation affecting the present.

questions.question: Complete: 'If you _____ me, I will help you with your homework.'
questions.explanation: First conditional for real future possibility. Present simple in if-clause.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'If I _____ more time, I would learn a new language.'
questions.explanation: Second conditional for hypothetical present situation. Past simple in if-clause.

title: Mixed Conditionals: Advanced Practice
description: Advanced practice with mixed conditional structures and variations.

questions.question: Complete the mixed conditional: 'If I _____ harder in school, I would have a better job now.'
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: past perfect in if-clause (past action) + would + base form in main clause (present result).

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'If she _____ the job, she would be living in Paris now.'
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: past perfect in if-clause (past decision) + would be + present participle (present continuous result).

title: Passive Voice: Comprehensive Practice
description: Master passive voice constructions across different tenses and contexts.

questions.question: Complete the passive voice: 'The report _____ by the manager yesterday.'
questions.explanation: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle. 'The report was written by the manager yesterday.'

questions.question: Choose the correct passive form: 'The building _____ next year.'
questions.explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle. 'The building will be built next year.'

questions.question: Complete: 'The letter _____ by the secretary every morning.'
questions.explanation: Present simple passive: is/are + past participle for habitual actions.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The project _____ by the team for months.'
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle for ongoing actions.

questions.question: Complete: 'The meeting _____ at 3 PM tomorrow.'
questions.explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle for scheduled events.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The car _____ by the mechanic right now.'
questions.explanation: Present continuous passive: is/are being + past participle for actions in progress.

questions.question: Complete: 'The book _____ by millions of readers.'
questions.explanation: Present simple passive: is/are + past participle for general statements.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The house _____ when we arrived.'
questions.explanation: Past continuous passive: was/were being + past participle for actions in progress in the past.

questions.question: Complete: 'The documents _____ by the lawyer yesterday.'
questions.explanation: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle for completed actions in the past.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'The problem _____ by the engineers next week.'
questions.explanation: Future passive: will be + past participle for future actions.

title: Reported Speech: Advanced Practice
description: Advanced practice with reported speech, including tense changes and reporting verbs.

questions.question: Complete the reported speech: 'I am studying English,' he said. → He said he _____ English.
questions.explanation: Present continuous changes to past continuous in reported speech: 'was studying'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'I will help you,' she said. → She said she _____ me.
questions.explanation: Future simple changes to would + base form in reported speech: 'would help'.

questions.question: Complete: 'I have finished my homework,' he said. → He said he _____ his homework.
questions.explanation: Present perfect changes to past perfect in reported speech: 'had finished'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'I can speak French,' she said. → She said she _____ French.
questions.explanation: Can changes to could in reported speech: 'could speak'.

questions.question: Complete: 'I went to the cinema yesterday,' he said. → He said he _____ to the cinema the day before.
questions.explanation: Past simple often changes to past perfect in reported speech: 'had gone'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'I must leave now,' she said. → She said she _____ leave then.
questions.explanation: Must changes to had to in reported speech: 'had to leave'.

questions.question: Complete: 'I am going to buy a car,' he said. → He said he _____ to buy a car.
questions.explanation: Be going to changes to was/were going to in reported speech: 'was going'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'I may come tomorrow,' she said. → She said she _____ come the next day.
questions.explanation: May changes to might in reported speech: 'might come'.

questions.question: Complete: 'I don't like coffee,' he said. → He said he _____ coffee.
questions.explanation: Present simple changes to past simple in reported speech: 'didn't like'.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'I have been working here for 5 years,' she said. → She said she _____ there for 5 years.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous changes to past perfect continuous in reported speech: 'had been working'.
